State of Maine
DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION
Testimony of Beth Lambert, Chief Teaching and Learning Officer
In Support of: L.D. 1701
An Act to Support the Implementation of Learning Standards and Results in Public Schools
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs
Sponsored by: Rep. Brennan
Co-Sponsored by: Senator Rafferty and Representatives Cloutier, Dodge, Gramlich, Mitchell, Moonen, Murphy and Sargent
Date: April 30, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Education and Cultural Affairs:
My name is Beth Lambert, and I serve as the Chief Teaching and Learning Officer at the Maine Department of Education. l am here today representing the Department, speaking in support of
the proposed amendment for L.D. 1701, An Act to Support the Implementation of Learning
Standards and Results in Public Schools. This bill would direct the Department to convene a workgroup to study the system of Maine Learning Results and make recommendations for improvement.
Learning standards in the United States have changed significantly over the past several
decades. Beginning in the 1980s and 1990s, there was a national movement to define clear expectations for what students should know and be able to do at each grade level. Maine joined this effort with the establishment of the Maine Learning Results in 1995, our first statewide academic standards across multiple content areas. These standards were intended to
provide clear statewide learning goals, while leaving curriculum decisions, such as instructional materials and teaching methods, to local schools and educators.
Since 1995, the Maine Learning Results have undergone several major updates: a revision in
2008, the adoption of the Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts and
Mathematic in 2011, and a full round of revision across all content areas between 2018-2020. Over this time, the standards have shifted from broad guiding frameworks to, at times, extremely detailed and specific documents. While some detail is important, overly granular standards risk being mistaken for curriculum, limiting local flexibility and innovation.
At the same time, our understanding of how students learn has continued to grow. Advances in learning science have deepened our understanding of cognitive development, motivation, and
1

engagement. It is critical that our state standards reflect this newer research and continue to meet the needs of Maine students and educators. The Maine Learning Results are reviewed on a rotating basis as required by Title 20-A, Chapter 222. However, the pace of reviewing eight content areas within a five-year cycle leaves little opportunity for deeper conversations about purpose, structure, and effectiveness. It limits our ability to step back and assess whether the standards are achieving their intended purpose, supporting effective teaching and learning, and remaining aligned with both the latest research and the evolving needs of Maine's students and communities. The recent passage of LD 74 that was signed on April 11, 2025 extended our review timeline from 5 to 7 years. This additional
time will allow the Maine DOE and a group of dedicated stakeholders to devote the time
necessary to review and support meaningful implementation in each content area, but not the System of Learning Results as a whole.
The Department supports the proposed amendment to LD 1701 because it makes space for an
important, comprehensive reflection. Convening a workgroup to study the Learning Results would allow a group of educators, experts, and curriculum leaders to look closely at the purpose of the Learning Results, ensure the structure supports local flexibility, and confirm that they are aligned with modern educational research and practice. Based on the workgroup's findings and recommendations, the Department would continue the regular review process going forward, strengthened by a clearer, and more focused vision for the Learning Results. For these reasons, the Department of Education is in support of L.D. 1701, An Act to Support
the Implementation of Learning Standards and Results in Public Schools. l am happy to answer
any questions the Committee may have, and I will be available for work sessions on this bill.

Testimony of Debra Mclntyre, Executive Director; on behalf of the members of the Maine Curriculum Leaders Association, testifying in support of LD 1701 An Act to Support the implementation of Learning Standards and Results in Public Schools, as amended by the sponson
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and members of the Education and Cultural Affairs
Committee, my name is Debra Mclntyre, and I am the Executive Director of the Maine Curriculum Leaders Association. On behalf of the members of MCLA, l offer testimony in support of LD 1701 An Act to Support the Implementation of Learning Standards and Results in
Public Schools, as amended by the sponsor.
The Learning Results sen/e as the foundation for educational planning, instruction, and assessment across Maine's public schools. They are integral to ensuring that all students have access to a high-quality, consistent education aligned with state standards and expectations.
However, as with any foundational system, periodic and thorough review is essential. LD 1701
recognizes the importance of evaluating both the process and structure by which these standards are developed, implemented, and updated.We do however, want to ensure that the
recent 7 year review cycle remains intact as stated in previous testimony. A broad and inclusive
approach to this review is not only appropriate, but necessary. Diverse voices--including those of educators, administrators and community leaders - must be heard to ensure the Learning Results reflect the evolving needs of our communities.
Those of us who need to use the standards to develop curriculum would greatly appreciate a common format and structure regardless of content area, especially at the elementary grades where educators may teach all content areas. Developmentally appropriate and cohesive
standards that build upon previous knowledge and skills is essential to designing an impactful curriculum that will support student achievement.
The Maine Curriculum Leaders Association (MCLA) strongly supports this bill and would be pleased to partner in this work. Our members bring direct experience with curriculum design,
implementation, and instructional leadership. We would welcome the opportunity to contribute to
a thoughtful and collaborative process that strengthens Maine's educational system.
Thank you for your consideration.

Testimony In Support Of LD 1701: An Act to Support the Implementation of Learning Standards and Results in Public
Schools Mallory Cook, Training and Early Educator Engagement Director, Maine Education Association
Before the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee April 30th, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and other members of the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee,
My name is Mallory Cook, and I have the pleasure of serving the nearly 24,000 members of the Maine Education Association as the Director of Training and Early Educator Engagement. I am here today to testify in support of LD 1701 (as amended): An Act to Support the Implementation of Learning Standards and Results in Public Schools.
Earlier this session, MEA supported LD 74, An Act to Update the System of Learning Results Review Timeline, as it allows for extended implementation periods and data-driven decision-making. Additionally, we often oppose bills that add graduation requirements when the content and skills are already covered in the Learning Results, or those requirements would supplant some other requirement. The workgroup proposed in LD 1701 would provide a necessary evaluation of our current Learning Results processes and offer opportunities for potential statutory changes that would support efficacy, interdisciplinary instruction, cultural relevance, and accessibility.
We appreciate the diverse voices included in the work group. It is essential to involve practitioners from all grade spans and content areas represented in the standards. A representative from the curriculum leaders can provide valuable feedback from their membership, while educational representatives who can speak to the diverse cultures, communities, and traditions in Maine will ensure accurate representation in the standards.
Through this process, we believe it would be beneficial to examine the processes and standards used in other states to consider other skills that are currently not standardized but should be. The state's Measure What Matters report might also be used to inform this work.
Thank you and I will do my best to answer any questions you may have.

TESTIMONY NEITHER FOR NOR AGAINST
L.D. 1701
AN ACT TO SUPPORT THE IMPLEMENTATION OF LEARNING STANDARDS AND RESULTS IN PUBLIC SCHOOLS
April 30, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Noonan Murphy, and members of the Joint Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs, I am Steven Bailey, the Executive Director of the Maine School Management Association, testifying on behalf of the legislative committees of the Maine School Boards Association and the Maine School Superintendents Association neither for nor against L.D. 1701, An Act to Support the Implementation of Learning Standards and Results in Public Schools.
Our associations appreciate this bill's goal of assisting districts with the implementation of the Maine Learning Results. Our associations and others have repeatedly shared that any changes to the Learning Results must be accompanied by resources to assist districts and ensure these changes make their way into classrooms.
This amended version of L.D. 1701 appears to recognize those concerns, and would provide for a broader examination of the purpose of the Learning Results, their overall accessibility, and the integration of particular perspectives across content areas. These are worthwhile goals that will help the state to rethink elements of these standards while considering ways to assist districts in their implementation.
Many superintendents are also curriculum experts, and we would ask that superintendents also be represented on this workgroup, as they can share their experience in developing curriculum and implementing it in classrooms while balancing limited district resources.

Steven W. Bailey
MSBA Executive Director

Eileen E. King
MSSA Executive Director
